entities.summary: Stephen Harry Crandall was a professor of mechanical engineering at MIT. He earned his master's degree in engineering at Stevens Institute of Technology in Hoboken, New Jersey and his Ph.D. from MIT. He joined the MIT faculty in 1946 and taught dynamics and strength of materials until his retirement in 1991. He was a prolific author of texts in solid mechanics, numerical methods, and random vibration. His mentor at MIT was J. P. Den Hartog. He was awarded the Timoshenko Medal in 1990 "in recognition of distinguished contributions to the field of applied mechanics." He was elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 1993.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a professor of mechanical engineering at MIT, Crandall's work on solid mechanics and numerical methods had significant regional impact in North America, influencing generations of engineers. His contributions to the field earned him prestigious awards, including the Timoshenko Medal.
